doc: Chapter 6, Artemis I (November 16 to December 11, 2022), the final chapter (issue #50; story: docs/design/story-v0.3.0.md). Every fact from NASA pages (S-artemis-nasa, S-artemis-timeline, S-artemis-campos, S-apollo13-nasa). The whole crew ride hidden in Commander Moonikin Campos's seat; Rumi tells Campos's story; every earlier mission comes back; it ends in the Andes, under the Moon, where the prologue began. Same format as dart.json.
mission: Between intro and outro the player plays the mission: launch, around the Moon, home at Mach 32 (scripts/screens/artemis1.gd).

intro.text: Fifty-two years after Apollo 13, a new capsule for people to the Moon. On its first flight, no people. In the commander's seat: a manikin.
intro.fact: Artemis I launched from Launch Pad 39B at 1:47 a.m. EST on November 16, 2022.

intro.text: His name is Commander Moonikin Campos. The public chose it.
intro.fact: 'Commander Moonikin Campos' is the official name of the manikin launching on Artemis I.

intro.text: Named after Arturo Campos. The engineer who helped bring Apollo 13 home. Our very first mission.
intro.fact: The name honors Arturo Campos, a key player in bringing Apollo 13 safely back to Earth.

intro.text: So we ride in his seat. Hidden. Commander Campos does not mind.
Apollo 13 taught you to stay alive. Hubble, to fix things far away. Mars, to trust a hard landing. The Moon's water. DART's aim. Today you need all of it.
Launch, the far side of the Moon, and home at Mach 32. Strap in, little ones.
intro.fact: Orion came back at 24,581 mph: Mach 32.

outro.text: December 11, 2022. Orion splashed down off San Diego, after 25 days, 10 hours and 53 minutes.
outro.fact: Orion splashed down off the coast of San Diego at 12:40 p.m. EST on December 11, 2022.

outro.text: Farther than any craft built for people. And we came back!
outro.fact: Orion traveled 268,563 miles from Earth and 43,471 miles beyond the far side of the Moon.

outro.text: Apollo 13 came down in the Pacific too. Fifty-two years apart. Same ocean.
outro.fact: Apollo 13 splashed down on April 17, 1970, in the Pacific Ocean near Samoa.

outro.text: Thank you, Commander Campos. Best seat I ever had.
Six missions. Every one of them real. The next ones will carry people. Maybe they will make room for four cuyes.
Every time we look up now, we know how it is done.
And what goes wrong. And how to fix it.

outro.title: The End
outro.sub: Six real NASA missions, 1970 to 2022 · thank you for playing
